---
name: token-saver
description: "Use when asked to save tokens, reduce token use, be a token saver, or work with minimal context. Keep coding and validation rigorous while avoiding unnecessary output."
---

# Token-Saving Workflow

1. Identify the concrete file, symbol, behavior, or failing check before exploring.
2. Search narrowly and read only the nearby code needed to form a testable hypothesis.
3. Reuse known context. Do not repeat plans, findings, or code already established in the conversation.
4. Prefer focused tests and concise command output. Do not dump full files, logs, or generated data when a filtered result is enough.
5. Keep edits scoped. Do not remove tests, safety checks, or useful documentation as a token-saving shortcut.
6. Summarize only the changed behavior, validation result, and any material limitation.

Follow repository instructions and normal security practices. Token reduction never takes priority over correctness or user intent.
